messages:
jessica: Heads-up — I'm seeing cross-request KV-store contamination on long-context runs (~10k tokens). Repro on dev fairly reliably when we do two sequential generate calls from same process. Partial blocks from request A show up in request B's prefix KV pages.

jessica: Example trace snippet (sanitized):
```
[kv_page 0x7f9d] owner=req-42 start_token=0 len=512 tag=0x8f2a
[kv_page 0x7f9d] owner=req-41 start_token=460 len=52 tag=0x7c11  <-- stale from prev request
```

nate: whoa. does this repro on main or a branch? any recent kernel/kernel-selection changes?

jessica: main@a1b2c3d — bisected partially, looks introduced around the batching/evict refactor we merged last week (maybe the slot reuse path).

priya: possible culprit: we moved to page-aligned appends but didn't always reset the page metadata when recycling. if the page->valid_len isn't cleared, readers can think old fragments belong to the new owner.

priya: quick check — do we pin request_id in the header? last time we relied on a separate tag store that race-y when pages flip between shards.

derek: i've seen memory creeping up too for long sessions. observed old tags still present in slab after eviction. small excerpt from profiler: `kv_pages.live++` without corresponding frees between requests.

jessica: repro steps I used:
1) start local runtime with `--kv-page-size=512 --reuse-pages=true`
2) send generate(req1) with ~6k tokens
3) immediately send generate(req2) with different prompt but same client id
4) inspect /debug/kv/pages for overlapping tags

nate: can you dump the page headers when swapping? a minimal patch that zeroes header fields on reuse would be a good quick experiment.

jessica: tried that — zeroing `owner` + `valid_len` stopped contamination in my run. Not sure if it regresses perf (might ping GC path).

priya: We should add an assertion in debug builds: if page.owner != current_request then page.valid_len must be 0. will help catch silent leaks.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-4021 — "KV-store cross-request contamination on long contexts" (assigned to eng-runtime).

derek: i'll open a small PR to zero headers on recycle + add debug asserts. will include a perf microbenchmark to show impact.

nate: also add a test that runs two back-to-back generates in the same process and checks no shared tokens in KV. integration-level only, keep it fast.

jessica: filing repro and raw traces in the ticket now. pushing a curated minimal repro to gist and linking in the issue.

priya: heads-up: we should also scan allocator for off-by-one when computing offsets — earlier bug where `start_token` used bytes instead of token count. that could explain the misalignment hints I saw.

derek: ack. i'll look at offset math and the kernel that writes KV frames. if it's wrong, might corrupt both alignment and cause stale reads.

nate: thanks all. priorities: 1) stop-gap zero headers on recycle, 2) debug assert + test, 3) deeper bisect on allocator offsets. please ping me when PRs are up. :thumbsup:

jessica: thanks — assigning follow-ups in the ticket, will coordinate canary once we have a fix.

ops-bot: Canary deploy attempted: canary-2026-11-03-09:22 failed healthcheck on runtime-3 (non-related crash). Logged under #DEPLOY-115.

priya: noted. once PR is in i'll run the repro against a local canary build and post results here.

derek: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987 (WIP) — added header-zeroing + asserts. please review.

nate: on it, will review & run perf bench.

jessica: great. will update the incident with a summary after we validate.
